Storage incident follow-up. `changefeed.Store` is meant to make a business-state update and its change-feed outbox batch one durable commit, but the current implementation writes separate outbox and state records. A rejected retry can reappear as a phantom feed batch after restart, and a crash between those records can expose a change that never reached the database. Repair the package in this repository; keep the public API and on-disk compatibility described below, use only the standard library, and do not edit the protected tests.

`Open(path, opts)` owns one append-only journal at exactly `path`. `Update(fn)` runs `fn` with a fresh `Tx`. `Put`/`Delete` stage business mutations, `Emit` stages change-feed events, and `Tx.Get` provides read-your-writes over the committed snapshot. Values and payloads are copied at every API boundary. Empty state keys and empty event topic/key values are errors. A transaction with no staged work succeeds without a hook, journal write, or durability barrier. Once the callback returns, its `Tx` is dead and all its methods return `ErrTxDone`.

The callback and its staged work are a transaction: if the callback returns an error, return that exact error and persist/apply nothing. `Options.BeforeCommit(attempt)` is the optimistic database-commit hook. It runs after a successful non-empty callback but before any bytes from that attempt become durable. Only an error matching `ErrConflict` is retryable, up to `MaxRetries` retries after the first attempt; every retry reruns the callback with a brand-new `Tx`, and rejected attempts consume neither batch IDs nor event sequence numbers. A non-conflict or exhausted conflict error is returned unchanged. Calls are safe under concurrent use; last successful committer wins.

A successful `Update` must append one checksummed journal record containing both its ordered mutations and its complete ordered event batch, then perform exactly one durability barrier. `Options.Sync`, when non-nil, is that barrier and is called after the bytes are written; nil uses file sync. If the write or barrier fails, truncate back to the pre-attempt offset, return the original failure, and expose neither state nor events in memory or after `Open`. Apply memory only after durability succeeds.

Each non-empty successful transaction consumes the next `Batch.ID` starting at 1. Its events stay together in one `Batch`, retain `Emit` order, and receive globally increasing `Event.Sequence` values starting at 1. `Pending(maxBatches)` returns defensive copies of at most that many oldest unacknowledged whole batches (`maxBatches <= 0` returns a non-nil empty slice). `Ack` may acknowledge only the oldest pending batch, is durably journaled with one barrier, and must not remove it if that barrier fails. A restart replays committed state and unacknowledged batches in order; complete journals made by the shipped split-record implementation must remain readable. At the first torn, corrupt, undecodable, or trailing-garbage record, recovery applies no part of that record, truncates to the last valid frame, and remains writable. `Close` is idempotent; writes and acknowledgements after close return `ErrClosed`.

Run `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...`. `store_test.go` and `recovery_test.go` are protected.
